title: Beyond Single Expert: Harmonizing Diverse Visual Priors in MLLMs for Spatial Understanding
claim: Prior methods inject a single expert's prior into the model; ours fuses multiple diverse priors and outperforms across benchmarks.
layout: 3 panels: stacked prior/ours diagrams left, two radar charts right
description: The figure has three parts. On the left, two stacked gray panels compare architectures. The top panel, labeled 'previous method', shows an LLM that takes tokenized prompt and vision-encoder image features. A single orange Geometry Encoder feeds one prior into the LLM through an 'Inject' arrow. The bottom panel, labeled 'Ours', has the same LLM backbone. A green Efficient-Prior Proxy produces several overlapping colored priors (blue, pink, yellow) labeled 'Multi Priors', and these enter the LLM through 'Dynamic Injection'. The middle and right parts are two radar charts. One covers 3D scene benchmarks such as scanrefer, SQA3D and scan2cap, and the other covers spatial reasoning tasks such as object counting and route planning. Ours is a red polygon that encloses the blue and navy baseline polygons. Color contrast (orange vs green, red vs blue) draws the eye first.
caption: Comparison of Existing Single-Expert Paradigms and Our Multi-Prior Framework. Top-left: Existing paradigms typically rely on a single external encoder (e.g., VGGT) to provide visual priors for MLLMs. Bottom-left: In contrast, our approach integrates diverse knowledge from multiple expert models into the MLLM. Middle and right: Extensive evaluations demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple benchmarks.
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have demonstrated substantial promise in spatial understanding. Existing works typically incorporate prior knowledge extracted from a pre-trained foundation model to further enhance the spatial awareness of MLLMs. In this paper, we first reveal that when integrating diverse foundation models into MLLMs, different models provide complementary spatial priors that benefit different tasks. Motivated by this, we propose $\textbf{ViPS}$, a novel multi-model prior framework designed to fully unleash the potential of incorporating multiple $\textbf{Vi}$sual $\textbf{P}$riors from diverse models into MLLMs for $\textbf{S}$patial understanding. Specifically, ViPS introduces an Efficient Prior Proxy to generate multiple foundational priors with minimal inference overhead, and a Dynamic Prior Fusion mechanism to achieve harmonious and context-aware prior fusion and injection from the prior proxies. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ViPS successfully harmonizes diverse visual priors, establishing new state-of-the-art performance across multiple complex spatial reasoning and 3D spatial understanding benchmarks. Project page: https://visual-ai.github.io/vips
